accepted.reason: The frosted bar's median contrast is above 8:1; the low tail is content scrolling under the blur.
The skeleton shimmer is a loading signal, and it stops under prefers-reduced-motion.
The pulse signals live activity (processing, typing, a running tool) and stops under prefers-reduced-motion.
DESIGN.md gives every overlay (dialog, open menu) a hairline plus shadow so it separates in both themes.
The hero story frames the chart's own card inside the hero section on purpose; the detector reads it as nested only since the chart carries its visually hidden data table.
Detector false positive: text clipped at the edge of a scroll box is read as missing padding.
iOS chrome: the top bar's inline title (h1) and an open sheet's title (h2) are both nav-bar titles at one size, and the sheet is modal over the page.

These shell stories declare no page title, so the only h1 is the top bar's inline nav-bar title (16px) over body-size sentence-case day headings (h2, 14px); the templated large-title hierarchy is held by the Templates/List golden stories.
The overview template's own 320px rail beside a body that runs on below the fold, shown on purpose by a three-screen body; the route scan takes the same row without an exception (docs/ROUTE-SCAN.md).
Carbon's inline notification carries a 3px severity bar on its left edge (cmn-alert, square corners); it is the status signal, not decoration.
Disabled text is exempt from WCAG 1.4.3 and is Carbon's disabled grey (text-disabled on the neutral fill); DESIGN.md keeps a disabled chosen cell and a disabled search legible, not at full contrast.

The list is a section body: its release headings (h3) sit under the host's own h2 (the sheet title, the Settings About section), which the standalone component story does not render; the Templates/Whats new golden stories hold the full hierarchy.

The golden lays the shell pieces side by side in bordered frames, as Carbon's UI Shell page does; the side nav and the header carry their own hairlines inside the frame, which the detector reads as nested cards.
The frame holds the phone tab bar, which is docked flush to the bottom edge by design (iOS tab bar, no inset).
Guardrail T5's demonstration: the text is cut off with an ellipsis on purpose, and cmnTooltip shows the full value on hover and focus.
